title: A book for people with lives
hook: written for someone living in the world, not a monastery
tomorrow: how do you add something to a life without wrecking it?

segments.voice: Last time, the Imitation closed: four books of short sayings, one carried each day. The line was a saying a day. Now a new book opens.

Can you be holy with a job, a family and a full calendar? A bishop named Francis de Sales answers with a story. In the old days, he writes, a flower seller named Glycera could take the same handful of flowers and arrange them so many different ways that the painter Pausias, trying to paint her bouquets, gave up. He couldn't keep up with her. Same flowers, a new arrangement every time. And de Sales, opening his book, says: that's me. Everything about devotion has been said already. So why write one more book?
screen: `A JOB, A FAMILY, A FULL CALENDAR.` → `GLYCERA AND HER FLOWERS.` → `WHY ONE MORE BOOK?`

segments.voice: Because of who it's for. Nearly everyone who has written about devotion, the preface says, wrote for people withdrawn from the world. De Sales wants the others: people in towns, in households, at court, whose lives keep them out among everyone else. Same flowers; a different table. People said it couldn't be done, that a devout life in the middle of ordinary life was impossible. He answers with nature. The mother-of-pearl lives in the sea without taking in a drop of salt water. Fresh springs rise near certain islands, out in the ocean. A little moth flies through flames without burning its wings. So a strong, steady soul, he says, can live in the world without taking on the world's taste. Then he names his reader. The whole Introduction to the Devout Life is written to one person, Philothea. And here's the detail to share tonight: he explains the name himself. It means a soul that loves God. He built the book from notes for a real person, he says, but the name opens the door to anyone who wants devotion. Which is the answer to the hook. Yes: holy, with the job and the family and the calendar still on the table.
screen: `NOT FOR THE MONASTERY.` · `THE PEARL IN SALT WATER.` · `PHILOTHEA: A SOUL THAT LOVES GOD.` · `ANYONE WHO WANTS DEVOTION.` · then, large: `FOR PEOPLE IN THE WORLD.`

segments.voice: Look at one object that belongs to your ordinary day: your keys, a coffee mug, a backpack, a work badge. Hold it or rest your eyes on it, and let it stand for the whole crowded life it opens into. If you pray, offer that life to God just as it is, salt water and all.
Philothea. The name Francis de Sales gives his reader: a soul that loves God, living out in the world.
Your line: for people in the world. The pearl doesn't have to leave the sea. A new book, opened.
